ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure 1 is a topographic profile of a certain continent, with oceans on both sides and a continent in the middle. The figure marks the positions near the equator and the tropics, and draws the atmospheric circulation above the continent; inside the continent is labeled “continental thermal low,” whose position is relatively northward, showing that at this time the center of the thermal low has moved northward with the direct solar point. Then reason: The continental thermal low being northward indicates that this is the Northern Hemisphere summer, corresponding to the Southern Hemisphere winter. Cape Town and the Cape of Good Hope are located at the southern end of Africa, south of about 30°S in the Southern Hemisphere. In the Southern Hemisphere winter, they are obviously affected by the westerly belt, often with overcast and rainy weather, and the nearby sea area has relatively large wind and waves. Therefore, “Cape Town has clear weather, and the sea area near the Cape of Good Hope is calm and tranquil” is inconsistent with the atmospheric circulation conditions shown in Figure 1 at this time.
